subject: VectorWeave partner validation — reference design & sandbox handoff
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@vectorweave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VectorWeave partner validation — reference design & sandbox handoff

Jamie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we want to move VectorWeave from architecture review to a short, focused partner validation sprint so we can produce a reference-design guide and a reproducible sandbox that customers can test. High-level ask: run the compatibility checks below in your dev sandbox and share logs + a short runbook for any workarounds.

Key validation items (target: 5 business days):
- End-to-end inference calls against Redwood hosted dev model (100–512 token windows)
- Multi-tenant request routing test (pass-through headers + tenant isolation)
- Failure modes: simulated preemption and model fallback response validation
- Throughput baseline at 4k RPS equivalent traffic pattern (burst smoothing)
- Secrets/KMS handshake and customer key rotation test (no PII persisted)

I attached an integration requirements worksheet and a sample Redwood config. Please confirm the sandbox endpoint and an engineer who will own the run. We'll kick off a short weekly sync while you run tests.

Deliverables we need back:
1) Test checklist with PASS/FAIL per case and short notes
2) Raw request/response logs for three representative scenarios (sanitized)
3) Short runbook (1–2 pages) describing steps to reproduce the failing cases and any recommended fixes

Can you confirm ownership and an ETA by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@vectorweave.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VectorWeave partner validation — reference design & sandbox handoff

Irene —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll own this and I will be the primary contact. We've allocated a small validation pod: me (engineering lead) and Priya (integration engineer) — Priya will reach out for any infra access. ETA: initial PASS/FAIL checklist and logs by Friday COB (12/11). Runbook will follow by next Wednesday (12/16).

Quick clarifications before we start:
- For the throughput baseline, do you want synthetic traffic from your end or a replay of our recorded traffic? We prefer replay where possible to be representative.
- For tenant isolation, should we use the three sample tenants in the attached worksheet or create new tenant IDs?

Attachments: small trace samples attached (trace1.gz stub).

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Friday to walk any early results.

—Jamie
Jamie Lopez
Head of Integrations | VectorWeave, Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@vectorweave.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VectorWeave partner validation — reference design & sandbox handoff

Jamie —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of technical notes from our side after reviewing your trace sample:
- Replay is fine for throughput (we can seed traffic from our side too). If you replay, please include early-termination cases (client cancelled) — we need to verify KV-cache cleanup.
- Tenant IDs: please use the three sample tenants in the worksheet but prefix them with vw- to avoid collisions with internal testing (e.g., vw-tenant-a).
- For keys/KMS: we will provide a short-lived test key via our sandbox KMS integration. Do NOT use customer keys in the sandbox run.

Also, heads-up on an expected failure mode: our runtime will intentionally preempt long running requests to simulate eviction; include a check that VectorWeave's client retries preserve idempotency and don't duplicate downstream actions. If you see duplicate tokens in logs, flag it as FAIL.

If you hit infra permission errors, open PNTR-2193 and tag us — we'll triage.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Partner Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@vectorweave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: VectorWeave partner validation — reference design & sandbox handoff

Jamie —

Appreciate the validation artifacts you shared in the Friday sync and the checklist the team filed. We're marking two quick items as P1 follow-ups: 1) model-fallback semantics for partial responses, and 2) a recommended client backoff pattern when preemption occurs. Can your team produce a 1-page advisory on both? That will let us finalize the reference design and the public-facing integration guide.

Once we have that advisory we'll schedule a partner sign-off review and then publish the reference-design repo (will add you as contributors).

Thanks again — excellent collaboration so far.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
